news.Title: Will Alphabet Stock Soar After Oct. 28? History Offers an Answer That’s Strikingly Clear.
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) has played a significant role in the artificial intelligence (AI) story so far, and that's helped supercharge revenue growth and stock performance. The company develops AI products and services, uses them to improve its own business, and offers them to customers through its Google Cloud unit.

Given high demand for AI capacity, Alphabet has been one of the key players involved in the infrastructure build-out. Alphabet, Amazon , Microsoft , and Meta Platforms together plan to spend more than $700 billion this year on the ramp-up. So, the pace of AI growth depends, to a certain degree, on these leading players.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

With this in mind, investors closely watch these companies as they are well-positioned to benefit from AI growth -- if the AI story continues to unfold as expected. And that brings us to the date of Oct. 28, which could represent a catalyst for Alphabet. Will the stock, which has climbed about 7% this year, soar after that date? History offers an answer that's strikingly clear.

Image source: Getty Images.

The strength of Google Search

Let's start off by considering Alphabet's path so far. The company built its solid billion-dollar revenue stream thanks to something that we all know well: Google Search . It has been steadily No. 1 in search, holding 90% of the market, and advertising across the Google platform has driven revenue over time. Advertisers, knowing we look for various types of information through Google, seek to reach us there about their products and services.

In the second quarter, Google advertising made up 68% of Alphabet's total $119 billion in revenue.

Though this clearly continues to be Alphabet's bread and butter, AI is progressively proving itself to be a powerful revenue driver for the company. Alphabet has developed its own family of large language models, Gemini, and is using this LLM to improve Google Search and the advertising experience -- as a result, advertisers may spend even more here in the future.

At the same time, Alphabet offers Gemini to customers through Google Cloud , and demand for this and other AI capabilities has skyrocketed. In the quarter, Gemini reported an 82% increase in Google Cloud revenue to more than $24 billion, driven by enterprise AI solutions and enterprise AI infrastructure.

Story Continues

Spending heavily to serve demand

But as I mentioned above, Alphabet is spending heavily to serve this demand. Capital expenditures totaled about $44 billion in the quarter to support the AI build-out, with 60% of the infrastructure investment in servers and 40% in data centers and networking.

Investors have been enthusiastic about the growth, but on occasion, they've worried about the depth and speed of the capex increases -- and that's weighed on Alphabet stock from time to time.

Now, let's consider the event coming up on Oct. 28 and what history tells us about stock performance. Alphabet is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings after the market closes. History tells us that, in the two weeks following the past four quarterly reports, Alphabet stock has advanced three times.

So, recent history has a strikingly clear message for us: Alphabet stock may soar after its upcoming earnings report. It's also important to note that the message regarding AI growth could support this. Demand has been strong throughout the AI boom, and tech companies such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and ASML Holding , which have already reported earnings, have spoken of ongoing solid demand.

Of course, the one area that may weigh on investors' minds continues to be the levels of capex. Some investors have worried that tech giants are overspending, so this concern could get in the way of a positive stock performance from Alphabet after its report.

What does all of this mean for you as an investor? History says Alphabet may soar after Oct. 28, but the most important thing to focus on is a company's long-term earnings prospects and stock performance potential. And here, there's reason to be optimistic about Alphabet, making it a great stock to own as this AI boom continues to unfold.

news.Title: Zacks Earnings Trends Highlights: Meta, Tesla, Nvidia, Micron and Alphabet
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 22, 2026 – Zacks Director of Research Sheraz Mian says, "We are off to a bit of a mixed start in the Q3 reporting cycle, with the growth pace and the revenue-beat percentage tracking modestly lower relative to the recent past."

Q3 Earnings Season Preview: Revenue Beats Lag, Momentum Holds

Note: The following is an excerpt from this week's Earnings Trends report. You can access the full report that contains detailed historical actual and estimates for the current and following periods, please click here>>>

We get into the heart of the Q3 earnings season this week, with more than 250 companies reporting results, including 73 S&P 500 members. By the end of this week, we will have seen Q3 results from 118 S&P 500 members, or almost a quarter of the index's total membership.

We are off to a bit of a mixed start in the Q3 reporting cycle, with the growth pace and the revenue-beat percentage tracking modestly lower relative to the recent past. That said, the sample of results from the 9% of S&P 500 members that have reported is heavily weighted toward the Finance sector, and these initial mixed trends may shift as we head into the heart of the earnings season in the days ahead.

This week's line-up of earnings releases is comprised of a fairly representative cohort of bellwether operators from a broad mix of sectors and industries, including two of the Mag 7 players, Meta Platforms and Tesla, and several other Tech players like Netflix, Texas Instruments, IBM, Spotify, and others. We will get results from air carriers (United, American, Southwest), railroad operators (CSX, Union Pacific), credit card issuers (American Express, Capital One, Synchrony), and many other blue chips like Procter & Gamble, GM, AT&T, Halliburton, and others.

We will have a definitive sense of how good or otherwise the Q3 earnings season has been by the end of this week.

Looking at overall expectations for the quarter, combining the actual results from the 45 S&P 500 members that have reported already with estimates for the still-to-come companies, Q3 earnings are currently expected to increase by +24.6% from the same period last year on +11.7% higher revenues, the 8th straight quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index.

The Tech sector remains a major growth contributor, but momentum is broad-based, with 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors on track for positive earnings growth in Q3. Importantly, the revisions trend remains positive and broad-based, highlighting a steadily improving outlook.

Story Continues

As noted earlier, the revisions trend has been positive, sustaining the favorable trend in place for almost a year. Estimates for Q3 increased after the quarter got underway, and we are seeing a similar trend at play for 2026 Q4 estimates.

This positive revisions behavior is not a new development; it extends a tailwind that has been building for nearly a year. The positive revisions were at first concentrated in Technology and, more recently, Energy, following Middle East supply disruptions. However, for 2026 Q4 and also what we saw for Q3, the constructive estimate revisions have broadened significantly, rising across 7 of the 16 Zacks sectors—including Aerospace, Construction, Industrials, Finance, and Transportation alongside Tech and Energy.

On the negative side, Q4 estimates remain under pressure for these 8 sectors – Conglomerates, Autos, Basic Materials, Consumer Staples, Consumer Discretionary, Medical, Business Services, and Retail. It is important to note that estimates for full-year 2027 have also been trending higher.

Sector Focus: Broad-Based Strength

Q3 earnings are expected to be above the year-earlier level for 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors, with 5 sectors expected to enjoy double-digit growth. The Conglomerates and Consumer Staples sectors are the only ones expected to have lower earnings in Q3 relative to the same period last year.

The 5 sectors expected to enjoy double-digit earnings growth in Q3 are Aerospace (up +160.5%), Energy (+122.2%), Tech (+43.7%), Basic Materials (+29.5%), Transportation (+9.6%), and Industrial Products (+13.5%).

Q3 earnings growth for the S&P 500 index drops to +20.1% from +24.6% once the Energy sector's contribution is excluded from the index. Excluding the Tech sector, Q3 earnings growth for the rest of the index drops to +14.4%.

For the Finance sector, which has dominated the reporting docket thus far, Q3 earnings are expected to be up +7.3% from the same period last year on +6.3% higher revenues.

With Meta META and Tesla TSLA on deck to report results this week, it is useful to take a look at expectations for the Mag 7 group as a whole. The expectation is that Q3 earnings for the Mag 7 will increase by +20.9% on +22.8% higher revenues.

Excluding the Mag 7 group's contribution, Q3 earnings for the rest of the index would actually modestly improve to +25.8% (from +24.6%).

The Q3 earnings and revenue growth rate drops to +21.1% from +43.7% once the substantial contributions from Nvidia NVDA, Micron MU and Alphabet GOOGL are excluded.

Q3 Earnings Season Scorecard

Through Friday, October 16th, we have seen Q3 results from 45 S&P 500 members, or 9% of the index's total membership. Total earnings for these companies are up +46.3% from the same period last year on +13.9% higher revenues, with 82.2% beating EPS estimates and 62.2% beating revenue estimates.

The very strong earnings and revenue growth pace for this group of 45 S&P 500 members is mostly due to Micron, whose Q3 earnings increased +1075.7% from the year-earlier level. Excluding Micron, Q3 earnings for the remaining 44 index members that have reported would be up +10.4%.

For the Finance sector, we now have Q3 results from 44.3% of the sector's market capitalization in the S&P 500 index. Total earnings for these Finance sector companies are up +10.6% from the same period last year on +8.6% higher revenues, with 80% beating EPS estimates and 50% beating revenue estimates.

Not only are the growth rates tracking below other recent periods, but Finance sector companies also seem to be struggling to beat consensus EPS and revenue estimates.

The Earnings Big Picture

As we noted earlier, estimates for full-year 2027 are experiencing the same positive and broad-based revisions trend that we noted earlier in the context of 2026 Q4.

news.Title: European stocks buckle as French yields cross 5% barrier
news.Content:
Investing.com - European equity bourses buckled under pressure on Thursday, dragged lower by a relentless sell-off in French sovereign debt, while a tech sector retreat overshadowed resilient earnings from consumer defensive heavyweights.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The pan-European STOXX 600 index traded 0.8% lower, surrendering modest gains from the previous session.

France's CAC 40 led continental declines, down over 1%, while Italy's FTSE MIB slipped 0.1%, Greece's Athens General Index decoupled from broader European losses, trading 1% higher despite nationwide civil disruptions..

The benchmark French 10-year yield broke cleanly above 5%, continuing its upward creep to trade at levels last witnessed during the 2002 sovereign market cycle.

Speaking late Wednesday, French President Emmanuel Macron pledged to prevent a repeat of last weekend's violent anti-government riots as fresh protests loom. However, limited political progress toward passing spending cuts for France's 5.4% GDP deficit has left international allocators fearful of an extended structural stalemate.

Social friction expanded across Southern Europe. Thousands of students and teachers marched across Greece on Wednesday demanding higher education funding, echoing demonstrations across the continent.

Meanwhile, in Italy, weekend cost-of-living demonstrations in Milan prompted Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni to enact tougher anti-rioting measures. Crucially, Italian BTP yields have avoided the severe penalty hitting French OATs.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Tech stocks slide on Meta capital restructuring and Asian spillover

Though social media giant Meta Platforms posted better-than-expected third-quarter revenue, global trading desks reacted with caution to its announcement of a new nonvoting share class.

The move, intended to provide Meta with flexible equity capital raising to finance its multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout, reignited anxieties over prospective shareholder dilution and escalating corporate capex.

Tracking broad-based overnight losses across Asian semiconductor supply chains, European tech peers ASML, ASM International, Infineon, and Soitec all fell between 3% and 5%.

Semiconductor assembly equipment provider BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) fell 3% despite a new share repurchase program and management expecting positive order momentum to carry into the fourth quarter.

Story Continues

Cushioning broader market losses were resilient results from defensive giants.

Food and beverage leader Nestlé reported higher-than-expected organic sales growth for the third quarter, signaling strong pricing power and volume recovery across its core global markets.

Investors also digested quarterly revenue figures from luxury heavyweight Hermès which fell over 7% after reporting a modest 5.5% rise in sales .

news.Title: Wall Street Firm Names Amazon Its Top Pick With More Than 30% Upside. Is the Stock a Buy?
news.Content:
Morgan Stanley recently tapped Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) as its "Top Pick," placing a $350 price target on the stock. Analyst Brian Nowak called Amazon a "Rule of 90" company, meaning its annual revenue growth rate and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization ( EBITDA ) margin could exceed 90%.The analyst said he sees five catalysts for the stock to climb higher.

First, Nowak sees Amazon's cloud computing unit, Amazon Web Services (AWS), growing faster than previously expected. He now expects AWS to grow by 47% next year and 42% in 2028, after Nvidia noted that Amazon is expected to buy 2 million of its graphics processing units (GPUs) over the next two years. The analyst also predicted that Amazon will spend a whopping $355 billion in capital expenditures in 2027 and $365 billion in 2028.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

In addition to AWS revenue nearly tripling from $128.7 billion in 2025 to $373.6 billion in 2028, Nowak also expects the segment's operating margins to expand. He sees them coming in at 42% in 2027 and 44% in 2028, helping lead to $16.50 in adjusted EPS in 2028. The analyst also thinks increased visibility into its AI model service, Bedrock, could help drive multiple expansion for the stock.

On the e-commerce side, Morgan Stanley sees Amazon becoming an AI shopping winner and expects it to eventually team up with Meta Platforms and its Muse AI agent, which it has initially been reluctant to do.

Finally, Nowak called out Amazon's use of robotics, noting that for every 10% of units processed through a robot-powered fulfillment center, Amazon can save between $2 billion and $4 billion a year. He said that Amazon's efficiency is expanding quicker than he initially modeled.

Is Amazon stock a buy?

Amazon is one of my favorite stocks right now and one I own. The company should continue to see AWS growth accelerate as its large AI infrastructure investments begin to kick in. It has large commitments from both Anthropic and OpenAI, with its backlog growing into the triple digits in Q2, ending the quarter at $496 billion. The company is getting a nice return on its chip and networking investments with a payback of less than three years, while locking in contracts for five years or more.

I think Amazon's AWS economics could improve even further if it can direct more of this business toward its own Trainum chips. In April, CEO Andy Jassy said its chip business has a revenue run rate of around $20 billion and is closer to $50 billion when including internal use. Meanwhile, rival Alphabet has said it is seeing a one-year payback on its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), so the opportunity is certainly there.

Story Continues

Regardless, Amazon has the best scale in the cloud computing space, and Jassy has said this could eventually become a $1 trillion revenue business.

I also feel that Amazon's e-commerce operations are underappreciated. The business continues to see strong sales growth despite an uneven consumer environment. At the same time, it has some attractive new growth initiatives, including expanding its logistics network to offer high-margin, less-than-truckload shipping. Meanwhile, the company has quietly become one of the largest digital advertisers on the planet, and it continues to see strong growth in this high-gross margin business.

Perhaps the most underestimated part of the Amazon story, though, is its leadership in robotics. The company is the largest manufacturer and user of robots in the world, with a fleet of over 1 million robots, all controlled by its DeepFleet AI model. This is creating significant operational efficiencies in its e-commerce operations, leading to profit growth that far exceeds revenue growth.

With the stock trading at a forward P/E of 25 times 2027 analyst estimates, Amazon trades at a huge discount to brick-and-mortar retailers like Walmart and Costco , making it a no-brainer buy in my view.

news.Title: Asian stocks sink to 3-month low on tech angst, Gulf tensions
news.Content:
By Jiaxing Li

HONG KONG, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Asian stocks retreated on Thursday as technology shares led a broad selloff, with Wall Street earnings failing to quell worries over soaring AI investment costs, while escalating Gulf ‌tensions boosted oil and weighed on risk sentiment.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slumped 1.8% to ‌the lowest level in nearly three months and was on track for a fourth straight week of decline.

Japan's Nikkei gave up earlier gains to trade ​2% lower, Korean shares tumbled more than 4%, while China's blue-chip CSI300 fell 2%, pushing it to the brink of a technical bear market. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index lost more than 3%.

Tech leaders in the region were among the biggest losers, with Japan's Tokyo Electron down more than 6%. Korea's SK Hynix and Samsung were down 5.7% and 4.2%, respectively, while Alibaba tumbled 6.5% in ‌Hong Kong.

In early European trading, the pan-region ⁠Euro Stoxx 50 futures declined 0.9%. U.S. stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis, dropped 0.8%.

Overnight, the tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a slightly higher close. Space X posted its first profit as ⁠a public company and Meta reported third-quarter revenue that beat expectations, easing fears over the payoff from massive AI spending.

The optimism quickly evaporated in Asia, however, as investors refocused on AI costs, with Meta's plan to issue non-voting Class C stock reviving concerns over mounting ​capital ​commitments.

"There's a lot of noise out there at the moment and ​investors are still digesting this morning's results," said Kyle ‌Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

"Also, we're really only at the start of the meaty part of earnings season, which is coming at the same time that investors are tackling the uncertainty from an upcoming Fed decision, geopolitical risks, and US mid-terms."

Those geopolitical concerns were reflected in oil markets. Brent crude rose more than 2% to $111.03 a barrel, near a five-month high, after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised the risk of wider conflict and supply disruptions in the Middle East.

A flight ‌to safety pushed benchmark U.S. Treasury yields lower, with the 10-year yield ​falling nearly 6 basis points to 5.0857% and the 30-year yield touching ​a one-week low of 5.3850%.

French government bonds also remained ​under pressure after the 10-year yield climbed above 5%, as investors looked for signs the government ‌can contain social unrest and bring spending under control.

Story Continues

In ​currencies, the dollar index, which tracks ​the greenback against a basket of currencies of other major trading partners, dipped to 101.57. The euro was little changed at $1.1242.

The yen ticked up to 157.55 after Deputy Bank of Japan Governor Ryozo Himino signalled his readiness ​to raise borrowing costs. The Korean won ‌was muted at 1324, after the Bank of Korea left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.00% on ​Thursday.

Gold eased to $4,067.5 per ounce. [GOL/]

Bitcoin fell 2.2% to $82,771.05, while ether was also 2.2% lower at $2,436.3.

(Reporting by Jiaxing Li ​in Hong Kong; Editing by Kate Mayberry and Shri Navaratnam)

news.Title: Meta Delivers Another Blowout Earnings Report. Here's What Investors Need To Know
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) came into its third-quarter earnings report, riding a bullish wave after its release of Muse, its AI personal agent that has topped the app download charts.

The launch of Muse and its frontier model, Muse Wonder, has helped dispel the notion that Meta is just an advertising business and alleviates one of the biggest risks facing the company, as nearly all of its revenue comes from advertising.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The third-quarter report shows the Facebook parent's momentum continuing to build, and it bodes well for its future. Here's what investors need to know about the latest report.

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Meta is executing across the board

It's hard to find a flaw in Meta's latest quarter. Revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, which topped expectations at $63.4 billion. On the bottom line, the company reported earnings per share of $3.83 due to the impact of its $18.59 billion settlement over litigation around teen health and social media and a $9.89 billion charge it took as part of that. Adjusted for that, it would have finished with $22.9 billion in operating income and $7.40 in earnings per share.

Meta's ad business continued to deliver strong results with ad impressions up 10% and the average price per ad up by 14%, showing the company is delivering results for advertisers.

The company also delivered those results with 15% fewer employees, as it cut its headcount by roughly 10,000 in layoffs earlier this year, freeing up more cash to invest in AI.

The company even sees a narrower loss in its AI-focused reality labs division, calling for a loss of $18 billion-$19 billion, which is still enormous, but is at least trending in the right direction. It forecast losses in that segment to narrow to around $15 billion next year, a clear positive sign.

2. Meta sounds more bullish than ever on the future

Meta's ad business is delivering blockbuster results, but the company also seems to have a swagger from its momentum in AI and the Muse launch that it didn't previously have.

Its CFO outlook commentary said, "Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization." The company also called for strong overall revenue growth to continue through 2027.

Story Continues

CEO Mark Zuckerberg also shared that more than 10 million people in North America had set up Muse personal agents, and the company expects to eventually have billions of Muse users. Zuckerberg essentially said that he thought Muse could double the company's revenue over time, saying he expected Muse to reach a higher average revenue per user than it earns from advertising in the U.S. He also noted shopping has been the most popular use case, which is clearly monetizable for a company that has the world's second-biggest advertising business, and has half of the world on its platforms.

3. Meta is issuing a stock split

For the first time since its 20212 IPO, Meta is splitting its stock. The company is issuing one share of a new Class C non-voting stock for each share of Class A and Class B supervoting shares.

Effectively, the stock dividend will act as a 2-for-1 split, and the company expects the share price to reflect that once the stock dividend is executed on Jan. 19, 2027.

Management argued that creating a new class of non-voting shares would give it more flexibility in raising cash and in employee compensation. Additionally, the board of directors sees it as a way to continue maximizing long-term shareholder value and to keep Mark Zuckerberg at the helm of Meta.

Though stock splits don't change the fundamentals of a stock, investors still like them, and this one seems deserved with Meta stock trading around $700/share.

Overall, with strong growth in the core business and the emergence of AI, Meta looks well-positioned for further growth, especially as the stock trades at a discount to the S&P 500.

news.Title: Meta sued in Australian class action over alleged social media harm to children
news.Content:
SYDNEY, Oct 22 (Reuters) - A class-action lawsuit has been filed in an Australian court against Meta ‌Platforms' Facebook and Instagram that alleges the social ‌media platforms exposed children to harmful content and kept them addicted ​through algorithms.

The lawsuit, filed in the Federal Court, Australia's second-highest, by law firm MinterEllison this month could be the first in Australia to blame social media for harming ‌its users, particularly children ⁠and teenagers.

• The class-action suit has been filed on behalf of eight plaintiffs, who ⁠allege they were harmed by Meta while they were under the age of 18, and are seeking compensation.

• "We are ​aware of ​this claim and we ​will defend ourselves vigorously," ‌a Meta spokesperson said by email.

• In a suppression order on Monday, the court prohibited the reporting of any information which could reveal the identity of the applicants, and the statement of claim.

• The lawsuit comes amid ‌rising tensions between Australia and ​Big Tech after a world-first ban ​on social media ​for children under 16, and newly proposed ‌rules that could let users ​switch off algorithm-driven ​content on their feeds.

• Meta in August agreed to pay $18 billion to settle with nearly all US ​states to ‌resolve claims it designed social media to addict ​children.

(Reporting by Renju Jose in Sydney; Editing by ​Christopher Cushing and Muralikumar Anantharaman)

news.Title: Lam Research: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.Content:
On its September 2026 quarterly earnings call, held on Oct. 21, 2026, Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) reported record quarterly revenue and profitability. Artificial intelligence workloads drive higher semiconductor complexity and boost demand for wafer fab equipment, which is the capital machinery used to manufacture chips. This structural shift expands the addressable market and creates long-term opportunities across memory and logic markets. Three key takeaways from the call stand out for long-term investors.

1. Advanced Dry Resist Technology Elevates Long-Term Revenue Projections

Lam Research is seeing increased adoption of its Aether dry resist technology, an advanced tool used for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography patterning in chip manufacturing. Customer demand for high bandwidth memory and logic chips led management to raise its cumulative revenue forecast for the product line by $1 billion.

As a result, we now expect cumulative Aether-related revenue to reach approximately $2.5 billion by the end of the decade, roughly $1 billion above our prior expectations.

-- Tim Archer, President and Chief Executive Officer

2. Maintenance and Service Division Growth Doubles Long-Term Targets

The Customer Support Business Group (CSBG), which provides maintenance, spare parts, and equipment upgrades for installed tools, is expanding rapidly as chipmakers run factories at high utilization rates. Full-year division growth is projected to reach more than twice its long-term target, supported by performance-based contracts and automation software.

Finally, turning to CSBG, we are set to exit calendar year 2026 with solid momentum, with annual revenue expected to grow more than 30% year-over-year.

3. AI Storage Architecture Shift Drives Additional NAND Wafer Capacity

Artificial intelligence models are forcing a redesign of flash memory storage tiers and creating demand for single-level cell (SLC) NAND, a low-latency memory format. Because SLC stores fewer bits per cell, chipmakers require significantly more wafer manufacturing capacity to deliver equivalent storage volume.

Said differently, for each percentage point mix shift of NAND bits to SLC class devices, approximately 2% more installed wafer capacity will be needed to support the same bit demand.

Looking Ahead

Artificial intelligence adoption is accelerating across enterprise and consumer markets and driving unprecedented demand for semiconductor manufacturing tools.

Story Continues

Underpinning our outlook for WFE growth is the continued rapid adoption of AI by enterprises and consumers.

A massive installed base and leadership in deposition and etch steps position the business to capture rising equipment intensity as chip designs shift to 3D scaling. Management is focused on resolving near-term supply chain constraints while expanding global manufacturing capacity to support long-term industry growth.

Our technology leadership, growing installed base, and strategic investments in product innovation and manufacturing capacity position Lam to capitalize on these inflections and drive sustained outperformance.

news.Title: Asian markets dip as investors weigh tech earnings, Gulf tensions
news.Content:
By Jiaxing Li

HONG KONG, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Asian stocks struggled to stay above water in early trade on Thursday, as tech earnings optimism provided only fleeting support amid lingering ‌concerns over AI and uncertainty in the Gulf.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan ‌was down 0.2%, on track for a fourth straight week of decline. Japan's Nikkei stock index gave up earlier gains to trade ​0.4% lower, while Korean shares were down more than 1%.

US stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis, were down 0.4% at 7,765.8. Overnight, the tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close as better-than-expected earnings reports from market heavyweights helped ease some concerns over the sustainability and profitability of massive AI build-outs.

Space X posted ‌its first profit as a public ⁠company, Meta reported third-quarter revenue that beat expectations, while AI server maker Super Micro forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin that both topped estimates.

However, Meta's plan to issue ⁠non-voting Class C common stock drew renewed scrutiny on AI spending.

"There's a lot of noise out there at the moment and investors are still digesting this morning's results," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

"Also, ​we're really ​only at the start of the meaty part of ​earnings season, which is coming at the ‌same time that investors are tackling the uncertainty from an upcoming Fed decision, geopolitical risks, and US mid-terms."

In a sign of subdued risk sentiment, the yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes was down 4.2 basis points at 5.1065%, while the yield on 30-year notes was at a one-week low of 5.3968%.

Meanwhile, Brent crude rose 1.1% to $110.03 a barrel, near a five-month high. The US ordered diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid ‌Houthi strikes, while the New York Times reported the ​US and Israeli militaries had developed specific plans for renewed attacks ​on Iran after the US midterm elections, ​which take place on November 3.

In currencies, the dollar index, which tracks the ‌greenback against a basket of currencies of other ​major trading partners, dipped to ​102.2. The euro was little changed at $1.1231.

news.Title: Meta: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.Content:
On its third quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 21, 2026, Meta (NASDAQ:META) announced the launch of its Muse personal agent, an artificial intelligence (AI) assistant designed for personal superintelligence. Rapid adoption of new AI tools and ad system upgrades is expanding user engagement and establishing new monetization paths. Three things management said stand out.

1. Muse Reaches 10 Million Users as Commerce Drives Adoption

Meta introduced its Muse personal agent, an AI assistant that executes tasks for users, and recorded rapid adoption driven by unexpected shopping volume. Building a large consumer network enables the company to generate transaction fees from business partners over time.

In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up Muse personal agents, Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number 1 in the App Store almost every day.

-- Mark Elliot Zuckerberg, Chief Executive Officer

2. Reality Labs Narrowing Losses to $15 Billion as Focus Shifts

Management is pacing investments in virtual reality (VR) hardware to prioritize software and personal agent models. Reducing operating losses in this segment's profit and loss (P&L) statement frees up capital to fund high-return AI infrastructure.

So with these factors combined, we expect that the P&L of Reality Labs to improve from here with operating loss coming down to approximately $15 billion next year and trending toward profitability from there.

3. First-Party AI Models Cut Content Processing Costs by Over 80%

Transitioning content processing to internal Muse models improves recommendation accuracy across social feeds while drastically lowering compute expenses. Lower unit costs strengthen profit margins as engagement scales across apps.

In offline evaluations, these models are outperforming our prior production models and are reducing per unit content processing costs by more than 80% across Instagram threads, Facebook, and ads.

-- Susan J. Li, Chief Financial Officer

Looking Ahead

Engagement and ad efficiency are accelerating across Meta's social platforms. Infrastructure scale and global distribution give the business room to fund AI tools while tracking compute efficiency.

The benefits our AI investments are delivering to the core business combined with emerging opportunities from model advances and product launches, position us to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027.

Story Continues

Deploying personal agents to billions of users positions the company for long-term network monetization.

If compute efficiency continues improving quickly for another few years, which we think is highly likely, then Muse will be highly profitable over the years.

news.Title: Amazon vs. Target: Where Should Long-Term Investors Put Their Money?
news.Content:
Deciding between e-commerce dominance and brick-and-mortar stability requires a close look at the numbers. In this article, we'll take a look at Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Target (NYSE:TGT) to see which stock is a better buy.

Amazon dominates digital commerce and cloud infrastructure, while Target focuses on an omnichannel approach with roughly 2,000 stores across the United States. While both compete for consumer dollars, their business models and growth trajectories differ significantly. This comparison analyzes their financials and risks to help you navigate these retail leaders.

The case for Amazon.com

Amazon operates a massive digital marketplace and is a prominent name among retail stocks through its global online store and Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud computing division. The company serves a diverse range of customers, including individual shoppers, third-party vendors, and enterprise technology teams. It continues to leverage its proprietary logistics network and high-margin advertising services to maintain its leadership in the global economy.

According to its latest annual report filed for FY 2025, revenue reached $716.9 billion, representing growth of nearly 12.4% compared to the previous year. This growth was accompanied by net income of $77.7 billion, which reflects a net margin of close to 10.8%.

Amazon has total cash of $122.9 billion against total debt of $251.6 billion. Its debt-to-equity ratio is 45.6%, and its operating cash flow is $161.4 billion.

The case for Target

Target is a general merchandise retailer that uses its physical stores as fulfillment hubs for its digital sales. The company has established strong commercial ties with partners like Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), CVS , Disney , Levi's , and Starbucks (NASDAQ:SBUX) to drive guest traffic. It also operates the Target Plus marketplace and the Shipt delivery service while navigating the conclusion of its partnership with Ulta Beauty .

Based on its latest annual report filed for FY 2025, revenue reached $104.8 billion, which was a decrease of nearly 1.7% from the prior year. The company reported net income of $3.7 billion for the period, resulting in a net margin of 3.5%.

Target's total cash is $5.4 billion against total debt of $19.2 billion. Its debt-to-equity ratio is 107.5%, while its operating cash flow is $8.7 billion.

Risk profile comparison

Amazon faces intense competition across multiple industries, including e-commerce and cloud services, from well-funded competitors with significant resources. Its international operations expose the business to various geopolitical and regulatory risks, such as trade disputes and local licensing requirements. The complexity of its global fulfillment network and a high reliance on third-party suppliers and shipping companies create additional operational challenges for the business.

Story Continues

Target is susceptible to shifts in consumer spending patterns and macroeconomic instability within the U.S. economy, including inflationary pressures. The company manages significant supply chain risks and inventory shrink, which refers to the loss of products due to theft or administrative errors. Additionally, it faces ongoing legal risks, including product liability claims.

Valuation comparison

The forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, which uses future earnings estimates, suggests Target is the more affordable option, and its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio also shows it trading at a lower multiple of sales.

Metric

Amazon.com

Target

Forward P/E

23.6x

15.6x

P/S ratio

3.4x

0.6x

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Between the two, I wouldn't hesitate to own Amazon. That's because if I were looking more in the traditional retail space, I would pick Walmart over Target, as I feel it's done a better job of integrating technology into its business and has an undervalued advertising arm it's building. And between Target and Amazon, the choice gets even easier for me.

While Amazon does have a retail platform, what's more interesting is its connection to artificial intelligence (AI), a market that will be immensely profitable. In 2026, the worldwide AI market is valued at $707 billion, but that's expected to jump to $1.9 trillion by 2032.

According to Statista, as of Q1 2026, Amazon is the global leader in cloud infrastructure via AWS, with 28% market share. The next-closest company is Microsoft , with a 21% market share. Amazon is also making its own chips, which helps it become more vertically integrated, achieve higher margins, and not rely on third-party suppliers. It's also integrating AI into its Alexa devices and has a stake in the start-up Anthropic, so Amazon has many ways to profit from AI. Between Target and Amazon, there's just a lot more money that Amazon can haul in, making it a stock I'd rather own for the long haul.

news.Title: U.S. stock futures drop as investors weigh Tesla, Meta earnings
news.Content:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures fell sharply in Asian trading on Thursday as Tesla shares slid despite upbeat quarterly results, as uncertainty over a potential merger with SpaceX and concerns about the cost of artificial intelligence investment weighed on sentiment.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

S&P 500 Futures fell 0.9% to 7,732.75 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures slid 1.6% to 29,517.25 points by 02:55 ET (06:55 GMT). Dow Jones Futures slipped 0.5% to 52,796.0 points.

The reports from the two companies, released after the regular market close, marked a key test for investor appetite for large-cap technology stocks as Wall Street moved deeper into the third-quarter earnings season.

Tesla shares fell nearly 5% in extended trading despite beating analysts' expectations for quarterly earnings and revenue.

Investors were concerned by the company's decision to cut its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to about $20 billion from an earlier projection of more than $25 billion.

SpaceX shares also fell more than 2% in extended trading. The decline came amid uncertainty over a possible combination of Tesla and SpaceX, both led by Elon Musk.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Musk said both firms had formed a special committee to explore a potential merger with Tesla, but no agreement had been reached on transaction terms, and there was no guarantee a deal would proceed.

The uncertainty followed a strong rally in SpaceX shares on Thursday after the rocket and satellite company reported robust quarterly results and flagged a potential merger with Tesla.

Meanwhile, Meta shares rose nearly 1% in post-market trading after reporting stronger-than-expected revenue and a positive outlook for the current quarter.

Meta reported earnings of $3.83 per share, ahead of the $3.57 expected by analysts, while revenue climbed 26% from a year earlier to $64.6 billion, exceeding estimates of $63.34 billion. Its results were supported by advertising growth and increased engagement across its platforms, although a large legal settlement added to quarterly costs.

In Wednesday's regular session, U.S. equities had drawn support from strong results from SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI).

The NASDAQ Composite rose 1.1% on Wednesday, while the S&P 500 gained 0.6% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended 0.7% higher.

Story Continues

Investors were also monitoring elevated oil prices and interest-rate risks. Brent crude traded above $110 a barrel in Asian trading Thursday amid geopolitical uncertainty, while U.S. inflation pressures have raised concerns about the Federal Reserve's policy outlook ahead of its meeting next week.

Attention now turns to Thursday's earnings from companies including Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG), Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC), Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT), and Honeywell (NASDAQ:HON).

news.Title: Lam Research (LRCX) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Transcript
news.Content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Wed, Oct. 21, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Vice President of Investor Relations - Ram Ganesh

President and Chief Executive Officer - Tim Archer

Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer - Doug Bettinger

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Please also note, today's event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Ram Ganesh, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Ram Ganesh: Thank you, and good afternoon, everyone. Welcome to the Lam Research quarterly earnings conference call. With me today are Tim Archer, President and Chief Executive Officer, and Doug Bettinger, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. During today's call, we will share our overview on the business environment, and we will review our financial results for the September 2026 quarter and our outlook for the December 2026 quarter. The press release detailing our financial results was distributed a little after 1:00 P.M. Pacific Time. The release and the accompanying presentation slides for today's call can be also found on the investor section of the company's website.

Today's presentation and Q&A include forward-looking statements based on our current beliefs, expectations, and assumptions. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties, and actual results could differ materially from those expressed or implied in such statements. For a discussion of factors that could cause actual results to differ materially, please refer to the risk factors in our most recently filed periodic reports on Form 10-K and Form 10-Q, and subsequent filings with the SEC and the cautionary statement in the accompanying presentation slides. Today's discussion of our financial results will be presented on a non-GAAP financial basis unless otherwise specified. A detailed reconciliation between GAAP and non-GAAP results can be found in the accompanying presentation slides.

This call is scheduled to last until 3:00 P.M. Pacific Time. A replay of this call will be made available later this afternoon on our website. With that, I will hand the call over to Tim.

Tim Archer: Thanks, Ram, and thank you to everyone joining us today. In the September quarter, Lam again delivered record revenue and profitability. Gross margin, operating margin, and EPS all reached new highs, with operating margin topping 40% for the first time. Our performance throughout the year reflects the broad strength of our product portfolio and a relentless focus on operational execution as AI continues to drive unprecedented semiconductor demand and increasing device complexity. Including the midpoint of our December quarter guidance, we expect calendar year 2026 systems revenue to grow well over 40% year-on-year. Rising deposition and etch intensity across all device types and advanced packaging solutions is continuing to drive greater opportunity for Lam.

Story Continues

Over the past few years, increasing device complexity and a push towards greater 3D scaling have driven a four-point expansion of our served available market, or SAM, as a percentage of WFE. When combined with share gains from products addressing this growing SAM, we expect 2026 to mark our third consecutive year of WFE outperformance. For calendar year 2026, we expect WFE in the mid $150 billion range. Our preliminary 2027 WFE outlook is for more than $200 billion of spending, with percentage growth led by DRAM, followed by leading-edge foundry logic and NAND.

As we move into calendar year 2027, we see clean room space availability and supply chain constraints for certain components continuing to limit chip makers and equipment companies' ability to fully meet end demand. We are actively working with our suppliers to accelerate their capacity expansion plans, and are confident Lam is well-positioned to deliver on the strong demand we see ahead. Underpinning our outlook for WFE growth is the continued rapid adoption of AI by enterprises and consumers. It is reported that average weekly token usage is up roughly 250-fold in the past 18 months. As AI moves increasingly towards autonomous agentic workflows, demand for compute, memory, and storage solutions continues to expand.

For example, in NAND, AI performance and economics are driving demand for multiple tiers of storage, each optimized for different workloads. QLC today provides cost-effective storage for rapidly growing AI data volumes. TLC storage is used as a high-bandwidth tier for context memory and KV cache workloads. And SLC class NAND is emerging for low latency, high-speed access in agentic AI. We believe adoption of an SLC storage tier could become a meaningful driver of NAND wafer capacity. Converting from TLC to SLC class devices reduces bits per device by roughly 3 times.

Said differently, for each percentage point mix shift of NAND bits to SLC class devices, approximately 2% more installed wafer capacity will be needed to support the same bit demand. Incremental growth in bit demand would further amplify wafer capacity requirements. We expect all three storage tiers to grow, increasing the value and strategic importance of NAND. We believe Lam is best positioned to benefit from this inflection. We have the industry's largest installed base of NAND systems and a comprehensive product portfolio spanning all critical deposition and etch steps. Any increase in NAND bit demand, whether satisfied through installed base upgrades or capacity additions, will generate additional need for Lam's tools and technology.

Foundry logic and DRAM are seeing a similar device-level evolution to satisfy AI's emerging performance requirements. From advanced patterning and backside power to next-generation packaging, we see billions of dollars of potential SAM expansion and share gain opportunities for Lam in the years ahead. We are seeing the impact of our targeted investments in foundry logic and DRAM products in our calendar year 2026 results. These two market segments have accounted for approximately 80% of Lam's systems revenue growth year-to-date. A good example is our focus on advanced patterning requirements for foundry logic and DRAM.

With each technology node bringing more stringent EUV pattern fidelity and defectivity requirements, Lam's Akara etch, conductor etch and Aether dry resist tools are being paired to deliver unprecedented scaling capability. Importantly, these tools are also helping improve the productivity of DRAM scaling at a time when maximizing fab output is a critical priority for our customers. Multiple chip makers are adopting Akara for its ability to etch very high aspect ratio features with exceptional profile control, while at the same time delivering up to a 50% reduction in wafer-to-wafer and lot-to-lot variability, and up to a 50% gain in wafer output per fab footprint.

Similarly, Lam's Aether dry resist solution has demonstrated sub-10 nanometer resolution at the highest pattern density and fidelity with High-NA EUV. It helps achieve this result while requiring 10% lower exposure dose, improving scanner productivity and reducing patterning cost per wafer. Aether solutions are already ramping in HBM high volume manufacturing with Low-NA EUV, and we see additional insertion opportunities ahead across both DRAM and foundry logic customers. As a result, we now expect cumulative Aether-related revenue to reach approximately $2.5 billion by the end of the decade, roughly $1 billion above our prior expectations. Backside power is another example of where Lam's strength in deposition and etch is evident.

Separating power and signal routing allows for thicker backside metallization to reduce resistance and improve power efficiency. Implementation increases process complexity, driving the need for more deposition, plating, and etch steps. As customers ramp backside power at 2 nanometer and below, our production-proven Vector, Sabre, and Flex tools are well-suited to the task. Vector provides industry-leading footprint density and wafer-to-wafer repeatability with its unique quad architecture. Sabre is the global industry benchmark for electroplating due to its high productivity and superior on-wafer performance. Flex delivers high throughput dielectric etch with low defect levels, leveraging its differentiated small volume chamber design and confined plasma.

New materials such as molybdenum are also being introduced to enable more efficient electrical connections between the backside and front side of the wafer. For this emerging application, our Halo tool is gaining traction by enabling both plasma and thermal processes within a single chamber while delivering industry-leading productivity. We are gaining share in this expanding backside power SAM opportunity and recently secured tool of record wins for all four products at a leading customer. In advanced packaging, our market-leading Syndion product is winning advanced logic in HBM TSV applications. Syndion's differentiated hardware design enables rapid process switching to deliver highly uniform TSV profiles, smooth sidewalls, and high volume productivity. Recently, we attained four new positions across multiple customers.

Our Striker ALD product also achieved multiple TSV liner wins due to the film's superior step coverage and low etch rate. Beyond TSV applications, we secured additional Vector and VECTOR TEOS 3D wins for high-adhesion bonding films and interdie gap fill applications by delivering lower defectivity for thick film deposition. With its high deposition and etch intensity, advanced packaging has become a major growth driver for Lam. For next-generation AI and high-performance computing devices, customers are increasingly turning their sights towards panel-level packaging to scale manufacturing. Our panel-level packaging portfolio continues to gain momentum across fan-out packaging, glass core substrates, and emerging substrate and interposer architectures.

To date, we have shipped panel plating systems to more than 20 customers worldwide across panel sizes ranging from 300 by 300 millimeter-600 by 600 millimeter. Customers continue to select our Kallisto platform for its differentiated coplanarity and plating uniformity performance across bumps, pillars, and redistribution layers. Kallisto is also well-positioned to benefit from increasing adoption of glass core substrates through emerging through-glass via applications. Given our customer engagement, installed base growth, and technology leadership, we expect to achieve panel-level packaging market share that surpasses the strong position we already hold in current wafer-level packaging. Finally, turning to CSBG, we are set to exit calendar year 2026 with solid momentum, with annual revenue expected to grow more than 30% year-over-year.

This is more than twice the rate of our long-term target set at our last Analyst Day. Growth is broad-based across upgrades, spares, and services, supported by high fab utilization and customers' continued focus on installed base efficiency. The value we are delivering with Equipment Intelligence and Dextro Cobots recently helped us secure performance-based service contracts with multiple memory manufacturers. We expect CSBG momentum to continue in calendar year 2027, with revenue growing over 15% year-over-year. To wrap up, we believe the industry is in the early stages of a multi-year investment cycle, with customer visibility extending through 2028. Increasing manufacturing complexity, new materials integration, and advanced packaging are driving higher deposition and etch intensity across device segments.

Our technology leadership, growing installed base, and strategic investments in product innovation and manufacturing capacity position Lam to capitalize on these inflections and drive sustained outperformance. Thank you, and here's Doug.
